sections.h2: How should a Houston owner approach a fast sale?
sections.html:
Three paths exist: a broker listing, a private sale, or a cash purchase. Houston is a market of its own, with 2,397,315 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate, so prices swing from street to street.

Owners occupy only 42.1% of Houston homes, so landlords, investors and first-time buyers all bid for houses. A cash proposal suits a house with deferred upkeep, storm damage, a tenant or a cloudy title. A listing fits a house that shows well.

  • Pull the deed and any survey, and find out whether your street has deed restrictions.
  • Check which appraisal district and taxing units cover the address.
  • Gather two written offers, each stating a closing date.

sections.h2: What do Houston's history and land rules mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Houston began on August 30, 1836, when two brothers advertised the Town of Houston. The Handbook of Texas says it became the state's largest city by 1930, that the Ship Channel opened in 1914, and that annexations in the late 1940s and later decades took it to 627 square miles by 2015. The Census Bureau lists 640.44 square miles of land for 2020.

The detail that matters most is the lack of zoning. The Handbook says voters rejected it and that subdivision deed restrictions steer most construction. Those private restrictions can limit what you build and how a lot is used, so read yours and disclose them to the buyer.

The city's planning department adds that a plat, a surveyed map of the lot, is required before building permits. It notes that single-family classification can include a duplex or a garage apartment under 900 square feet unless the deed restrictions forbid it. Houston also reviews plats in an area about five miles beyond its limits, where its permit and inspection rules do not apply.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Houston owners and renters?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows a $277,800 midpoint home value for 2020 to 2024, with $2,240 in monthly costs for owners who carry a mortgage. The city has 930,404 households.

sections.h2: How does the Harris Central Appraisal District affect a sale?
sections.html:
The Harris Central Appraisal District values most Houston property for tax, and its site lets owners file protests, renditions and homestead exemptions online. It also offers an Exemption Wizard and a deed protection feature that lets you register your home with the Harris County Clerk to help guard against deed fraud.

The Comptroller's calendar gives the yearly beat. Appraisals are pegged to January 1. Homestead notices start about April 1, and the protest deadline is May 15 or 30 days past the notice, whichever is later. If the board's ruling disappoints, an owner can take the case to district court or binding arbitration, or to the State Office of Administrative Hearings once the board value passes $1,000,000. Appealing owners generally still pay the undisputed part of the tax on time.

  • Once the exemption is active, a homestead's appraised value can rise no more than 10% in a year.
  • Heirs missing from the recorded deed must supply an ownership affidavit, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to get the exemption.
  • A new owner who closes after January 1 can apply for the exemption for what remains of that year when the seller never did.

Check your tax bill to confirm which district and taxing units cover your parcel.

sections.h2: Which Houston neighborhoods and job centers shape what buyers want?
sections.html:
The Handbook of Texas traces Houston's spread through developer-built suburbs: Houston Heights and Pasadena in 1892, Bellaire in 1911, West University Place in 1919, and River Oaks in the mid-1920s. Those names still anchor listing descriptions, and buyers often search by them, though you should check whether a given address sits inside the city or in a separate municipality.

Jobs pull buyers toward particular corridors. The Handbook calls the Texas Medical Center the world's largest medical complex, with about 106,000 employees in 2016, and describes the Ship Channel refineries and petrochemical plants that made Houston an energy capital. Add a 27.2-minute average commute from QuickFacts and a drive-time pitch becomes part of your selling story: tell buyers how long it takes to reach the medical center, downtown or the channel from your front door.

Schools matter too. The Handbook says a free school system began in 1877 and became the Houston Independent School District in 1924. Confirm which district serves your address before you list, and say so in the listing.

sections.h2: Does flood history matter when selling in Houston?
sections.html:
Yes. Buyers and lenders ask about it. The Handbook of Texas describes paving and rapid runoff as sources of flooding, and says severe floods in 1929 and 1935 led to the Harris County Flood Control District and later to the Addicks and Barker reservoirs.

The city's planning department says flood mitigation, drainage, water and sewer are outside the Planning Commission's plat review, so a plat does not settle a house's flood risk. Ask the city and the county for flood records on your address, and collect repair records and insurance claims to share with buyers.

The Handbook also cites about 48 inches of yearly rainfall, high humidity and summer averages near 94 degrees, conditions that wear on roofs, siding and air conditioning. A cash buyer will take storm damage as is, and a clear paper trail helps both sides agree on a price.

sections.h2: What do tenants, heirs and tax debt change in a Houston sale?
sections.html:
Renters first: the usual written notice to vacate is three days unless the lease sets another period, and an eviction suit starts in justice court. The State Law Library puts the hearing 10 to 21 days after filing. Appeals to county court must come within five days of the judgment, and the writ of possession waits six days after final judgment.

Inherited house? The state repealed its inheritance tax effective September 1, 2015, according to a Comptroller notice. A probate case should open within four years of a death. The small estate affidavit route is reserved for estates of up to $75,000 apart from the homestead.

If taxes are behind, the lien that attached on January 1 stays on the house, and penalty and interest start February 1. A taxing unit can sue and sell the property at auction. County clerks record deeds, and a recorded plat can be requested from the Harris County Clerk's records office using the contact details on the city's plat page.

faqs.a: Census figures: 640.44 square miles of land in 2020, 2,397,315 residents in 2025. Confirm the county and appraisal district for your own address before relying on a tax figure.
No citywide zoning exists. The Handbook of Texas says voters rejected it. Private deed restrictions and the city's plat and permit rules still apply, so read your restrictions.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Houston property value?
faqs.a: Yes. Go to the appraisal review board by May 15, or up to 30 days after your notice arrives if that is later. The Harris Central Appraisal District site offers online filing.

faqs.q: Where do I find the plat for my lot?
faqs.a: Plats are filed with the Harris County Clerk's records office after approval. The city's planning site also has a map viewer and a Plat Tracker for searching by address.
It is a midpoint for the whole city in the 2020 to 2024 survey. Rely on written offers or an appraisal for your own house.
